Hands cultivate a garden with care.
Pexels · 7729129
Earth Day in everyday choices
There is more than one way to reduce everyday waste. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful
starting points.
One reason is that changing one repeat purchase can reduce waste over time. For instance, we bring a reusable bag and refill a
bottle. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that local knowledge makes shared action more effective. For example, we check the local recycling rules before
sorting materials. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need
different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Discuss the claim that more preparation always helps people reduce everyday waste. Support a qualified position with two concrete
examples. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the
situation; discuss changing one repeat purchase can reduce waste over time with an example; discuss local knowledge makes
shared action more effective with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
